hero.label: Microkernel · Lean 4 · Rust · Formally Verified
hero.subtitle_line1: Every kernel transition is an executable pure function.
hero.subtitle_line2: Every invariant is machine-checked by the Lean type-checker.
hero.h1: seLe4n — A Formally Verified Microkernel Written in Lean 4

about.title: What is seLe4n?
about.lead: seLe4n is a capability-based microkernel whose kernel model is written entirely in Lean 4 with machine-checked proofs, complemented by safe Rust syscall wrappers for user-space programs. It targets the Raspberry Pi 5 (ARM64 / BCM2712) as its first hardware platform.
about.why_microkernel_text: Microkernels minimize the trusted computing base by running only essential services in kernel space — scheduling, IPC, capability management, and memory control. Everything else (drivers, filesystems, networking) runs in user space. This reduces attack surface and makes formal verification tractable: every line of the Lean kernel model can be reasoned about mathematically.
about.why_lean_text: Lean 4 is both a general-purpose programming language and an interactive theorem prover. seLe4n leverages this duality: the kernel is executable code whose properties are machine-checked at compile time. There is no separate specification language and no translation step between the Lean model and its executable code; the hardware boundary beneath it — the Rust HAL behind the FFI bridge's @[extern] functions — is a documented trusted contract. If it compiles, the proofs hold.
about.how_it_works_title: How It Works: Build → Freeze → Execute
about.how_it_works_p1: seLe4n employs a three-phase architecture. During the Build phase, an IntermediateState wrapping SystemState with invariant witnesses is constructed through pure builder operations (createObject, registerInterface, markRunnable, withTaint). Each builder operation preserves four structural invariants. During the Freeze phase, the one-way freeze function converts the builder state into a FrozenSystemState where all RHTable fields become FrozenMap structures (hash → index + contiguous array) and CNode slots become CNodeRadix flat radix arrays with zero-hash O(1) lookup. During the Execute phase, frozen counterparts exist for the value-only mutations of 18 of the kernel’s 47 syscalls (pinned by frozenOpCoverage_count); structural builder-phase operations and live-scheduler/cache-maintenance operations have none. In the frozen state the index map is never modified, all Fin accesses are within bounds by construction, and no fuel or dynamic resizing is needed. The frozen phase is proved equivalent to the builder phase but is not yet the syscall dispatch path: API.lean still runs over the live state.
about.how_it_works_p2: All three phases are unified by the KernelM monad, defined as σ → Except ε (α × σ) — a state-transformer with explicit error handling. The freeze step carries machine-checked lookup-equivalence proofs — every key readable in the builder state reads identically in the frozen state — and a commutativity layer establishes frozen_op(freeze(s)) = freeze(builder_op(s)) for value-only mutations, ensuring the frozen execution phase is semantically equivalent to the builder phase. Every transition is deterministic: given the same input state and system call, you always get the same output state.
about.what_different_text: seLe4n unifies implementation and proof in a single language — no separate proof assistant, no translation layer, no semantic gap. Each subsystem follows an Operations/Invariant split: executable transitions live in Operations.lean, and their machine-checked proofs live alongside in Invariant.lean. The type-checker enforces that every invariant holds across every operation.
about.status_text: seLe4n is an active research project at version 0.37.19. The kernel model is feature-complete with 47 syscalls spanning IPC, scheduling, capabilities, memory management, notifications, information-flow control, and a service registry. A companion Rust workspace provides safe, no_std wrappers for the kernel's syscall ABI. The hardware binding for the Raspberry Pi 5 is complete — HAL, GIC-400 interrupt controller, ARM Generic Timer, ARMv8 page tables, and QEMU boot — the syscall path that allocates nothing (WS-ZA) closed at v0.37.0, and the active workstreams are the bare-metal boot path (WS-BP) and carved objects that live in their untyped's own memory (WS-UC), with a syscall ABI that is seL4's own (WS-SX) planned next.
about.created_with: Created thoughtfully with the help of Claude and Codex.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.lead: seLe4n follows a layered contract model. Each subsystem's invariant proofs compose upward into a unified apiInvariantBundle that covers the entire kernel. A companion Rust workspace provides safe, no_std syscall wrappers above the API surface.
architecture.diagram_aria: seLe4n architecture diagram showing Rust user-space wrappers, kernel API surface, and layered subsystems down to platform bindings
architecture.prelude_desc: Typed identifiers (ObjId, ThreadId, DomainId, Priority, CPtr, Slot, ASID, VAddr, PAddr, RegName, etc.) each with Hashable + LawfulHashable instances. The KernelM monad, register files, memory regions, and timer configuration. Sentinel value 0 reserved for ObjId, ThreadId, ServiceId, and CPtr with identity theorems.
architecture.object_model_desc: 1The SystemState record aggregates all stores into a single immutable snapshot — its object store a verified RHTable keyed by ObjId.
architecture.scheduler_desc: 3,425 theorems across 68 files spanning core operations, per-core SMP dispatch, priority inheritance, and liveness proofs. Each core keeps only its run queue's ends (RunQueueEnds): the ends of the queue of runnable threads and of each priority bucket, and the highest queued priority. The links live in the TCBs, as seL4's tcbSchedNext/tcbSchedPrev, so insert, remove and membership are O(1) and selection starts at the highest queued bucket. Priority + EDF scheduling with domain-aware partitioning. schedulerWellFormed structural invariant. Operations split into Core, Preservation, and Selection. PriorityInheritance with blocking graph analysis and bounded inversion. Liveness proofs including WCRT bounds and domain-rotation guarantees.
architecture.capability_desc: 781 theorems across 22 modules. A CNode's slots are a fixed array of 2radixWidth cells written in place, as seL4's cte_t array, and each slot holds its own derivation links (LinkField: parent, first child, next and previous sibling), so the slot is the derivation-tree node, as in seL4's mapping database — proven to agree with the ghost tree (cdtLinksAgree). Invariant proofs split into Authority (43 theorems), Defs (65 theorems), and a Preservation suite (281 theorems across 13 files). A delete splices its slot out of the tree (spliceNode), and cspaceRevokeCdtFinalising revokes as seL4's cteRevoke does: it deletes the source's first child until none is left.
architecture.ipc_desc: Deeply modularized across 171 files with 6,837 theorems. Intrusive dual-queue endpoints split into Core, Transport, and WithCaps. 652 structural invariant proofs, 42 endpoint preservation theorems, and 27 capability transfer proofs. Operations decomposed into CapTransfer, Endpoint, SchedulerLemmas, Donation, and Timeout.
architecture.robin_hood_desc: Verified Robin Hood hash table implementation with 275 theorems across 10 modules. RHTable provides O(1) amortized insert, lookup, and erase with open addressing and linear probing. 62 bridge theorems connect the implementation to HashMap-compatible semantics. 64 preservation proofs and 52 lookup correctness theorems. Imported by Model.Object.Types — the verified foundation for all kernel hash-based data structures.
architecture.info_flow_desc: 1,912 theorems across 28 deeply modularized files. Enforcement split into Soundness and Wrappers. Invariant proofs decomposed into Composition, Helpers, and Operations. A non-interference proof for each of the 36 kernel steps, 46 more for cross-core operations, and proven reflexivity and transitivity.
architecture.service_desc: 52 theorems across 5 files. A capability-indexed service registry: a registration names an interface and an endpoint capability and is recorded on the endpoint it names, so a lookup is one object read. Operations re-exports the registry operations, Interface defines service contracts, and Registry registers, revokes and looks up services, with its proofs in Registry.Invariant. The kernel keeps no dependency graph: dependency policy is left, as in seL4, to a user-level service manager.
architecture.platform_desc: PlatformBinding typeclass defines runtime, boot, and interrupt boundary contracts. BootBoundaryContract captures per-platform boot guarantees. Concrete bindings for a simulator, QEMU's virt board (the kernel's first executed boot, on four PEs) and the Raspberry Pi 5 (BCM2712 memory map, GIC-400 constants, ARM64 config, 48-bit VA / 40-bit PA).
architecture.rust_desc: Four no_std Rust crates: three user-space crates provide ergonomic, fully safe, typed wrappers over the whole verified 47-syscall seLe4n ABI, while the kernel-side sele4n-hal supplies the ARM64 hardware abstraction layer. sele4n-types defines a 47-variant SyscallId enum, 16 #[repr(transparent)] newtype identifiers, a 61-variant KernelError enum (60 mirroring the Lean inductive plus a Rust-only forward-compatibility sentinel), and bitmask-based AccessRights — all with #![deny(unsafe_code)]. sele4n-abi handles ARM64 register encoding/decoding, IPC buffer overflow, and MessageInfo bitfield packing — with exactly one unsafe operation: the inline svc #0 instruction in trap.rs. sele4n-sys exposes typed wrappers for IPC (send/receive/call/reply/replyRecv), CSpace (mint/copy/move/delete/revoke), lifecycle (untyped retype/reset), VSpace (map/unmap with W^X enforcement, page-table map/unmap), service registry (register/revoke/query), TCB management (suspend/resume/setPriority/setSpace/setAffinity/setFaultHandler), and notification (signal/wait) — zero unsafe code.

comparison.title: seLe4n vs Traditional Verified Kernels
comparison.lead: seLe4n builds on decades of capability-based microkernel research while introducing architectural improvements enabled by the Lean 4 proof framework.
comparison.language_sele4n: Lean 4 for both implementation and proofs
comparison.verification_gap_sele4n: No spec-to-code gap in the Lean model — proofs live alongside code; the hardware boundary is a documented trusted contract
comparison.ipc_queuing_trad: One queue per endpoint, its direction in the endpoint state
comparison.cdt_trad: Mapping database linked through the slots
comparison.user_space_bindings_trad: C headers with manual register marshalling
comparison.data_structures_sele4n: Verified Robin Hood tables for keyed maps (275 proofs); queues linked through the TCBs
comparison.ipc_queuing_sele4n: Separate send and receive queues linked through the TCBs, O(1) mid-queue removal
comparison.scheduling_sele4n: Priority + EDF with domain-aware partitioning
comparison.cdt_sele4n: The same links in each slot, proven to agree with a ghost derivation tree
comparison.info_flow_sele4n: N-domain two-dimensional labels with per-endpoint policies
comparison.service_mgmt_sele4n: Service registry recorded on the serving endpoint; dependency policy left to user level
comparison.revocation_sele4n: The same loop, checked before any write; a delete never refuses on derived capabilities
comparison.syscall_boundary_sele4n: Verified decode with roundtrip + determinism proofs
comparison.user_space_bindings_sele4n: Safe Rust wrappers — all 47 syscalls, typed capabilities, zero unsafe in sele4n-sys
comparison.state_model_sele4n: Immutable records, pure functional transitions
comparison.execution_model_sele4n: Three-phase Build → Freeze → Execute with FrozenMap + CNodeRadix
comparison.object_composition_trad: Static object tables, manual pointer management
comparison.object_composition_sele4n: Composable typed capabilities with bitmask rights, 1,527 structural theorems

features.title: Key Innovations
features.lead: seLe4n introduces architectural improvements across every subsystem, with O(1) data structures and machine-checked correctness at every layer.
features.o1_text: Hot paths touch a constant number of words. The object store, VSpace mappings, ASID table, priority-bucket ends and service interface registry are verified Robin Hood tables with 275 theorems; the kernel's queues — run queues, endpoint and notification queues, reply waiters — are linked through the TCBs, and a CNode's slots are a fixed array, as in seL4. At freeze time the tables become FrozenMap and CNodeRadix structures for deterministic O(1) access. Typed identifiers have Hashable + LawfulHashable instances.
features.robin_hood_text: Traditional verified kernels rely on linked lists with O(n) traversal. seLe4n builds on a ground-up verified Robin Hood hash table — 275 theorems across 10 modules, with 62 bridge theorems connecting the implementation to HashMap-compatible semantics. It backs the object store and every keyed map the kernel keeps.
features.scheduler_text: Where traditional kernels use priority-based round-robin, seLe4n combines Priority + EDF with domain-aware partitioning. Each core's RunQueueEnds records the highest queued priority, so selection starts at the top bucket rather than scanning every thread, and the queue's links live in the TCBs. The schedulerWellFormed structural invariant rolls into schedulerInvariantBundle, machine-checked across all 3,425 scheduler theorems, including priority inheritance and liveness proofs with WCRT bounds.
features.ipc_text: seL4 keeps one queue per endpoint, its direction in the endpoint's state. seLe4n endpoints keep separate sendQ/receiveQ ends, linked through the TCBs, with O(1) mid-queue removal. A message is registers and a badge (IpcMessage): capabilities travel as addresses in the sender's frame and are resolved at the rendezvous (resolveExtraCaps), as seL4's lookupExtraCaps. WithCaps proves the transfer — 6,837 theorems including call-reply-recv composition proofs.
features.cdt_text: As in seL4's mapping database, each CNode slot holds its derivation links — parent, first child, next and previous sibling — so the slot is the node and moving a capability moves its place in the tree. seLe4n proves the links agree with a ghost derivation tree (cdtLinksAgree). A delete splices its slot out and re-derives its children from its parent (spliceNode), so it never depends on whether the capability has derivations; cspaceRevokeCdtFinalising is seL4's cteRevoke loop, its check read before any write.
features.info_flow_text: Where traditional kernels use a binary high/low partition, seLe4n implements a parameterized N-domain framework with two-dimensional labels (confidentiality + integrity). DomainFlowPolicy supports arbitrary flow topologies with proven reflexivity and transitivity. A non-interference proof for each of the 36 kernel steps, stated over the ObservableState projection of what a domain can observe.
features.service_text: Traditional microkernels have no kernel-level service concept. seLe4n adds a capability-indexed service registry: a registration names an interface and an endpoint capability and is recorded on the endpoint itself, so lookupServiceByRecordedRegistration is one object read. Every registration names a live endpoint by construction (registryEndpointValid_holds), and dependency policy is left, as in seL4, to a user-level service manager — 52 theorems across the service subsystem.
features.arch_text: Where traditional kernels leave register parsing unverified, seLe4n verifies the hardware-software boundary end-to-end. RegisterDecode (45 decode-layer proofs) and SyscallArgDecode (98 proofs, round-trip proofs included) ensure no data is misinterpreted at the trap boundary. TlbModel adds flush-consistency proofs for the memory subsystem.
features.invariant_text: Each subsystem proves its own invariant bundle. Bundles compose upward: coreIpcInvariantBundle, ipcSchedulerCouplingInvariantBundle, lifecycleCompositionInvariantBundle, and vspaceInvariantBundle all roll up into proofLayerInvariantBundle, exposed as the unified apiInvariantBundle. A base-case theorem proves the bundle holds for the default (empty) state.
features.composable_objects_text: Where traditional kernels use static object tables with manual pointer management, seLe4n’s 10 kernel object types compose through typed Capability references with bitmask-based AccessRightSet. Every object lives in one store in SystemState, a verified RHTable keyed by ObjId, and the CapDerivationTree enables composable revocation across the entire object graph — 1,527 theorems total.
features.rust_text: Where traditional kernels expose C headers with manual register marshalling, seLe4n provides four no_std Rust crates — three user-space crates with fully safe, typed APIs over the verified 47-syscall ABI, plus the kernel-side sele4n-hal (ARM64 hardware abstraction layer). sele4n-sys introduces phantom-typed Cap<Obj, Rts> capabilities with compile-time rights tracking and W^X enforcement. The three user-space crates have zero unsafe except the svc #0 trap instruction in sele4n-abi; the HAL confines hardware access to scoped unsafe blocks.

security.title: Security Model
security.lead: Security is woven into every layer of seLe4n through formal information-flow control, capability-based access mediation, and a documented threat model.
security.threat_model_title: Threat Model & Security Boundaries
security.ifc_text: seLe4n enforces information-flow security at the kernel level through 1,912 theorems across 28 modules. The DomainFlowPolicy framework provides security guarantees that go beyond traditional binary high/low models:
security.ifc_item1: A non-interference proof for every kernel step — one for each of the 36 constructors of the NonInterferenceStep inductive, and 46 more for cross-core operations under SMP
security.ifc_item6: 55 operations classified by enforcement level, 69 once the per-core cross-core wrappers join them
security.ifc_item8: Legacy embedding theorem proves the generic system subsumes the original
security.cap_text: All resource access is mediated through capabilities stored in CNode slots. The capability derivation tree tracks all parent-child relationships:
security.cap_item1: Fixed slot arrays: a CNode's slots are written in place, as seL4's cte_t
security.cap_item2: Revocation as seL4's cteRevoke: the first child is deleted until none is left
security.cap_item3: Derivation links in each slot, proven to agree with the derivation tree
security.cap_item5: Policy-checked wrappers: endpointSendDualChecked, cspaceMintChecked, registerServiceChecked
security.cap_item6: Sentinel ID rejection at IPC boundaries prevents ghost queue entries
security.protected_item4: Repository integrity and CI policy state
security.threat_item1: External attacker: Public repo access, dependency injection
security.control_item1: Expanded .gitignore secret/artifact denylist
security.control_item2: SHA-256 verified elan installer downloads
security.control_item3: Tier-3 anchor checks against CI workflow semantics
security.control_item4: Blocking CodeQL gate with Tier-0 workflow-policy checks

verification.title: Verification & Testing
verification.lead: seLe4n employs a multi-tiered verification strategy combining Lean’s type-checker with runtime testing, ensuring correctness from proof to execution.
verification.use_smoke: Minimum PR requirement (includes the host Rust lane and docs sync)
verification.tier0_text: Forbidden-marker scans ensure zero sorry and zero axiom across all production code. Documentation link validation, sync checks, and formatting enforcement. The first line of defense.
verification.tier1_text: Full Lean compilation of the 605 production Lean modules. All 24,025 theorems in them are type-checked, and the in-tree testing framework builds alongside, outside these figures. Every invariant proof, every bridge lemma, every preservation theorem is verified by the Lean type-checker. If it compiles, the proofs hold.
verification.tier2_text: Trace sequence probes validate executable behavior against formal semantics. The negative-state suite tests malformed input rejection across IPC, capabilities, endpoints, and CSpace mutations. Determinism validation runs the trace executable twice and requires identical output. Information-flow runtime checks verify enforcement wrappers.
verification.tier3_text: Anchors every named theorem and invariant to the proof surface. Verifies that all documented claims in the Claim & Evidence Index are backed by actual code. Ensures no proof regressions across refactoring. The full correctness gate for PRs.
verification.tier4_text: Scenario-seed replay from the canonical catalog, staged experimental candidate validation, and long-running invariant probes. An opt-in Tier 5 harness cross-checks the Lean oracle against the Rust oracle. Catches subtle regressions that slip through faster tiers.
verification.low_item2: Trivially true for unchanged state returns

api.title: API Surface
api.lead: The kernel exposes a stable public API through SeLe4n/Kernel/API.lean via the unified syscallEntry / syscallEntryChecked dispatch path. All 47 syscall-facing operations are routed through capability-gated dispatch with information-flow enforcement. The production entry point syscallEntryChecked enforces flow policies; the unchecked syscallEntry is retained for backward compatibility with existing proofs. All 47 syscalls have corresponding safe Rust wrappers in sele4n-sys.

structure.title: Project Structure
structure.lead: 605 Lean modules, 72 test and CI scripts, and 257 documentation files with specifications, ADRs, and roadmaps.

getting_started.title: Getting Started
getting_started.lead: Whether you want to explore the kernel model, contribute proofs, or understand the architecture — here is how to get up and running.
getting_started.step2_text: The setup script installs elan (the Lean version manager) with SHA-256 checksum verification and the pinned Lean 4.28.0 toolchain.
getting_started.step3_text: Build the kernel and its staged modules. All 24,025 theorems across its 605 production Lean modules are checked; lake build alone builds the Main closure, so the staged hardware-binding and lock-primitive modules need the second target. The in-tree testing framework builds too, outside these figures. Zero sorry, zero axiom.
getting_started.step4_text: Start with the smoke test (minimum for PRs), then run the full suite for invariant work.
getting_started.step5_text: The rust/ workspace provides safe, no_std wrappers around the whole seLe4n syscall surface (all 47 syscalls). Builds on both ARM64 (real trap) and x86_64 (mock trap for host-based testing). After any change under rust/, run both Rust lanes: the host lane cannot see the HAL's aarch64-only code, which the cross-build lane builds for its real target.
getting_started.contributing_intro: seLe4n welcomes contributors. Before submitting a PR:
getting_started.contributing_item1: Read the Contributing Guide and Development Docs
getting_started.contributing_item2: Identify which area of the project your change addresses
getting_started.contributing_item3: Run ./scripts/test_smoke.sh at minimum; test_full.sh for theorem changes
getting_started.contributing_item4: Update invariants and theorems together with code changes
getting_started.contributing_item5: Keep PRs focused on one coherent unit of work
getting_started.contributing_item6: State transitions must have explicit success or failure outcomes

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.lead: Development is organized into milestones covering kernel semantics, audit remediation, performance, and hardware binding. Here is where the project stands.
roadmap.semantic_text: Scheduler semantics, capability/CSpace operations, IPC seeds, waiting handshake, lifecycle/retype, capability composition, service graphs, architecture boundary assumptions, and initial audit remediation.
roadmap.audit_text: Four complete audit portfolios: comprehensive audit, model/docs/maintainability, test validity and proof gaps, and test/CI and kernel hardening. All findings closed.
roadmap.remediation_text: Intrusive dual-queue IPC with message transfer verification. Untyped memory retype with watermark tracking. Information-flow completeness — ObservableState projection. Proof gap closure across all operations.
roadmap.perf_text: Migrated all hot paths to O(1) hash-based structures. 14 performance audit findings eliminated. Typed identifier Hashable instances, object store HashMap, ASID resolution table, RunQueue restructure, CNode slot HashMap, VSpace mapping HashMap, IPC dual-queue + notification, graph traversal optimization, and information-flow projection optimization. 400+ theorems re-verified. On the hottest paths WS-ZA has since moved to seL4's own layout: queues linked through the TCBs and fixed CNode slot arrays.
roadmap.freeze_text: Implemented the Build → Freeze → Execute pipeline with commutativity lemmas over the frozen store — the frozen operation set, 12 at completion, has grown since — establishing frozen-phase semantic equivalence. FrozenOps subsystem with typed lookups, value-only mutations, and queue operations — all with isolation and preservation proofs.
roadmap.syscall_expansion_text: Expanded from 14 to 25 syscalls: added notification (Signal/Wait), compound IPC (ReplyRecv), scheduling context (Configure/Bind/Unbind), and TCB management (Suspend/Resume/SetPriority/SetMCPriority/SetIPCBuffer). Unified syscallEntry / syscallEntryChecked dispatch path with capability-gated routing. Rust ABI hardening with the SyscallId enum (since grown to 47 variants).
roadmap.rust_desc: Three no_std Rust crates (sele4n-types, sele4n-abi, sele4n-sys) providing safe wrappers around all 25 syscalls of the surface as it stood at completion (it has since grown to 47, and the wrappers cover all of them) including notification, compound IPC, scheduling contexts, and TCB management. Phantom-typed capabilities, ARM64 register ABI layer, W^X enforcement, IPC buffer overflow handling. unsafe confined to the svc #0 trap instruction.
roadmap.refinement_text:
Model fidelity — badge bitmask, per-thread registers, multi-level CSpace.
Invariant quality — tautology reclassification, adapter proof hooks.
Testing expansion — oracle, probe, and fixture coverage.
Cleanup — dead code removal, legacy/dual-queue resolution.
roadmap.rpi5_text: Hardware binding portfolio (WS-AG, AG1–AG10) delivered: the sele4n-hal bare-metal crate, GIC-400 interrupt dispatch, ARM Generic Timer, ARMv8 page tables with ASID management, exception and interrupt models, cache coherency and speculation barriers, an FFI bridge that now carries 83 @[extern] functions, and QEMU boot verification. BCM2712 memory map with 48-bit VA / 40-bit PA address space.
roadmap.smp_text:
Per-core scheduler, IPC, and TLB-shootdown semantics. Verified lock primitives — ticket lock and RwLock with refinement bridges — with deadlock freedom and serializability proofs. Cross-core non-interference and per-core information-flow projection.
Target: v1.0.0 — a bootable verified SMP microkernel on all four Raspberry Pi 5 cores. Phases SM0–SM9 have landed, closing with declassification completion; WS-RR (SMP release readiness) closed at v0.35.203, and SM10, the release closure, now waits on WS-BP, the bare-metal boot path: BP0–BP7 have landed and BP8 is under way — the Lean-linked image boots on all four PEs of QEMU’s virt board on every PR.
roadmap.convergence_text: Proof-to-platform convergence. Map model observability assumptions to RPi5 adapter obligations. Document unresolved security debt for side-channel follow-up.
roadmap.za_title: WS-ZA: A Syscall That Allocates Nothing
roadmap.za_text: seL4 allocates nothing on a syscall. When the workstream was registered, the exerciser that counts heap allocations on QEMU’s virt read 118 for one notification signal. The workstream closed at v0.37.0: every kernel entry and every syscall now reads 0, at first call and in steady state, except a retype’s carve, which allocates exactly its object’s cells. Run, endpoint, notification and reply-waiter queues are linked through the TCBs, a CNode’s slots are a fixed array holding their own derivation links, and objects change in their slots.

footer.brand_text: A microkernel written in Lean 4 with machine-checked proofs.
